subtopics.title: Vision and Six Pillars
subtopics.summary: Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2026-27 as her record ninth consecutive budget, prepared in the newly inaugurated Kartavya Bhawan. It is framed as a Yuva Shakti-driven blueprint anchored in the Viksit Bharat Vision and guided by three Kartavyas. Six pillars of growth organise the agenda across manufacturing, MSMEs, infrastructure, financial stability and city economic regions.
facts: Presented by Nirmala Sitharaman as her record 9th consecutive Union Budget
Framed as a Yuva Shakti-driven blueprint anchored in the Viksit Bharat Vision
Three Kartavyas: Sustain Economic Growth; Fulfill Aspirations; Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas
First-ever Union Budget tabled on a Sunday, a Parliamentary first
Pillar 1: Scaling up manufacturing in seven strategic sectors
Pillar 2: Rejuvenating legacy industrial sectors to boost productivity and competitiveness
Pillar 3: Creating champion MSMEs to strengthen the backbone of the economy
Pillar 4: Delivering infrastructure development across the country
Pillar 5: Ensuring long-term security and stability in economic and financial systems
Pillar 6: Developing city economic regions to drive regional growth and urban development

subtopics.title: Manufacturing, Industry and Infrastructure
subtopics.summary: The budget pairs manufacturing schemes for biopharma, semiconductors, containers and critical minerals with infrastructure measures for freight, carbon capture and urban growth. SHAKTI aims to make India a global bio-pharmaceutical manufacturing hub, while the Rare Earth Corridor aims to secure the mining-to-manufacturing value chain. Funds for MSMEs, carbon capture and City Economic Regions complete the package.
facts: Biopharma SHAKTI: outlay of 2,10,000 crore over 5 years to build a global bio-pharma manufacturing hub
SHAKTI stands for Strategy for Healthcare Advancement through Knowledge, Technology & Innovation
Bio-economy target: USD 300 Bn by 2030; contributes 4.25% of GDP
Semiconductor Mission 2.0 shifts focus from assembly to higher-value manufacturing and indigenous IP
Container scheme aims to reduce dependence on Chinese imports
Rare Earth Corridor across Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
Dankuni (West Bengal) to Surat (Gujarat) freight corridor proposed for East-West logistics
SME Growth Fund of 10,000 crore to scale MSMEs into Champion enterprises
CCUS outlay of 20,000 crore to decarbonise hard-to-abate sectors like steel and cement
City Economic Regions: 5,000 crore per region over 5 years

subtopics.title: Agriculture, Services and Women-led Growth
subtopics.summary: Agriculture measures centre on Bharat-VISTAAR, an AI-based platform for accessing farm resources, and on higher-margin plantation crops. Creative and service sectors get talent pipelines and the Orange Economy is promoted, while foreign cloud providers using Indian data centres receive a tax holiday. Women-led development gets community-owned retail outlets and STEM hostels for girls.
facts: Bharat-VISTAAR: Virtually Integrated System to Access Agricultural Resources
A multi-lingual AI-based platform integrating AgriStack portals and ICAR's agricultural practices
Special support for sandalwood, agar trees, walnuts and almonds
Target: Global Brand Status for Indian cashew and cocoa by 2030
Content Creator Labs in 15,000 Schools and 500 Colleges for the AVGC sector
Orange Economy coined by Ivan Duque Marquez and Felipe Buitrago in their 2013 work
Orange Economy value comes mainly from intellectual property, ideas and cultural expression
Cloud services tax holiday for foreign companies using Indian data centres until 2047
SHE Marts: community-owned retail outlets for women's SHGs
One dedicated girls' hostel in each district to retain female students in STEM

subtopics.title: Taxation and Fiscal Framework
subtopics.summary: The budget retained existing income tax slabs for FY 2026-27 and replaces the 1961 Act with a new Income Tax Act 2025 from 1 April 2026. Tax changes include a uniform 2% TCS on LRS remittances and a Minimum Alternate Tax cut to 14%. The fiscal framework sets a deficit target of 4.3% of GDP, record capex of 12.2 lakh crore and a total outlay of 53.47 lakh crore.
facts: New Income Tax Act 2025 replaces the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 to reduce litigation
Existing income tax slabs retained for FY 2026-27
TCS rationalised to a uniform 2% on overseas tours, education and medical remittances under LRS
MAT proposed as a final tax, rate cut to 14% from 15%; non-residents exempted
LRS introduced in 2004 by RBI; limit of USD 2,50,000 per financial year
Projections for FY 2026-27: 10.5% nominal GDP growth and around 7% real GDP growth
Fiscal deficit target for FY 2026-27 is 4.3% of GDP
Debt estimated to decline to 55.6% in BE 2026-27 from 56.1% in RE 2025-26
Record capex of 12.2 lakh crore; total outlay of 53.47 lakh crore
TCS on LRS is governed under Section 206C of the Income Tax Act 1961

subtopics.title: Budget Process and Parliament
subtopics.summary: Article 112 requires the annual financial statement to be laid before Parliament, although the word 'Budget' does not appear in the Constitution. The budget is prepared by the Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs with NITI Aayog and ministries. Money Bills start in Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha can only return them within 14 days without any power to vote on demands for grants.
facts: Article 112 (Part V): annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government
The term 'Budget' is not mentioned anywhere in the Constitution
Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs prepares it with NITI Aayog
Six stages: presentation, general discussion, scrutiny, voting on demands, appropriation bill, finance bill
Money/Finance Bill involving taxation is introduced only in Lok Sabha
Rajya Sabha must return a Money/Finance Bill within 14 days
Railway Budget was presented separately for 92 years, merged with the Union Budget in 2017
India's first budget was presented on 7 April 1860 by James Wilson
First post-independence Union Budget presented by R.K. Shanmukham Chetty on 26 Nov 1947
Budget announcement moved to the 1st working day of February from 2017

quizzes.passage: Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget for the financial year 2026-27, which is her ninth consecutive Union Budget. The budget was prepared in a newly inaugurated building, and the government has presented it as a blueprint driven by Yuva Shakti. The budget is guided by a set of principles that the government has set out for the country's economy. The budget was tabled on a day of the week that had never before been used for a Union Budget, which made it a first for Parliament. The agenda is organised into six pillars of growth, and the pillars cover several different parts of the economy. Each pillar addresses a separate area, and together they form the core of the government's growth agenda for the coming year. The budget is a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government for a financial year, and it is presented in Parliament. Preparing the budget involves several departments and bodies, and the presentation is one step in a longer process that the government follows each year. The budget also reflects the government's approach to growth for the coming year, as set out in its official budget material. Taken as a whole, the budget is a blueprint for the country's economic growth in the year ahead.

quizzes.passage: The budget set out measures for agriculture, services and women-led development, which it presented as separate parts of its agenda. For farmers, it proposed an AI-based platform that gives access to agricultural resources in several languages. It also announced special support for crops that can help farmers diversify into higher-margin plantation crops. The budget set a goal for certain Indian farm exports to earn a stronger global brand, which is intended to enhance export realisation. In services, the budget proposes Content Creator Labs in schools and colleges to build a talent pipeline for a booming sector. The budget also promotes the Orange Economy, which is grouped under services, technology and tourism. For women-led development, the budget proposed SHE Marts, through which women's self-help groups can sell products directly. It also proposed a girls' hostel in each district, to help more female students stay in science, technology, engineering and mathematics courses. Each of these proposals is presented as a separate initiative within the budget. The budget describes these measures as steps toward growth in agriculture, services and women-led development. Taken together, they are part of the government's wider growth agenda for the year ahead. Each of these areas is discussed separately in the budget, and each has its own set of measures.

quizzes.passage: The Constitution requires the government to present an annual statement of its estimated receipts and expenditure for each financial year before both Houses of Parliament. The word budget itself does not appear anywhere in the Constitution, although the annual statement is treated as the budget. The process has several stages. It begins with presentation of the statement, followed by general discussion and scrutiny by departmental committees. Then Parliament votes on demands for grants, passes an appropriation bill and passes a finance bill. The preparation of the statement is handled by a division of the finance ministry, which works with other ministries and a government policy body. Money bills and finance bills follow special procedures, and the two houses of Parliament have different roles in them. Budgets have been presented in India for well over a century, and the earliest one came before independence. The annual statement sets out the government's expected revenue and spending for the year ahead, and it also records the actual receipts and expenditure of the closing year. The budget is presented in Parliament on a date fixed for the purpose. Parliament examines the statement in a series of stages each year, and each stage has its own role in the process.
